label: Forward entry and a usable rotational plant
effort: Turn a short forward entry into a low hip-led roundhouse while controlling forward drift.
brief: The limiting demand is receiving forward momentum without a reaching, locked support knee. Supporting tasks connect a short approach to rotation, unilateral forward acceptance, the plant-to-chamber link, rear-leg propulsion and a controlled forward finish.
marker: valid E2 attempts out of four per leg with one support-foot entry step, no extra brake step, free foot/pelvic rotation and a finish inside the marked segment.

e.name: Two-step approach quarter-turn jump to stick
e.execution: Take exactly two short controlled approach steps, gather onto two feet and jump through a turn of no more than 45 degrees. Land aligned on two feet and hold 2 s. The approach plus flight fits within 2 m, with 2 m recovery clear.
e.job: Convert small forward arrival into leg-driven rotation before the direct kick task.
e.gate: Use shorter approach steps and less turn instead if the gather stalls or landing drifts beyond the boundary.
e.novelty: A counted two-step approach/gather feeds the turn; earlier rotational broad jumps started still.

e.name: Forward step-in low roundhouse
e.execution: With the kicking leg initially rear, step the support foot a short distance forward, accept weight with a soft knee, let that foot turn and launch the low rear-leg roundhouse. Recoil and recover within the same 2 m work segment. No run-up or pad.
e.job: Directly translate controlled forward arrival into pelvic rotation and free-leg acceleration.
e.gate: Use a shorter/slower step instead for overstriding or extra braking steps; preserve controlled brisk kick intent after the qualified plant.
e.novelty: Full kick after a forward receiving step rather than stationary, parallel, lateral-shuffle or bounce initiation.

e.name: Forward bound to opposite-leg stick
e.execution: From a short stationary split stance, push forward from one leg into one modest bound and land on the opposite leg. Stay facing forward and hold 2 s; no turn or second bound. Flight fits within 1.5 m.
e.job: Prepare the receiving leg for forward bodyweight without simultaneously demanding a rotating landing.
e.gate: Use a shorter bound or light free-toe assist at the finish instead if the receiving knee stiffens or another hop is needed.
e.novelty: Unilateral forward projection to the opposite support leg; previous opposite-leg bounds were lateral.

e.name: Forward plant to low rotational chamber
e.execution: Make one short forward receiving step onto the support foot, turn that foot/pelvis together and lift the free folded knee into a low rotational chamber. Hold 2 s, then set the foot down. Do not extend the lower leg.
e.job: Isolate acceptance-to-free-thigh timing inside the forward-entry kick without another full extension dose.
e.gate: Shorten the step/chamber instead if the athlete rises onto a rigid knee or has to hop.
e.novelty: Grounded forward plant feeds a held rotational chamber; distinct from Class 2 plant-to-stance and Class 5 lateral crossover chamber.

e.name: Rear-leg power step to opposite-leg plant
e.execution: Start in a compact split stance with the named leg rear. Drive from that rear hip/forefoot into one brisk forward step onto the other leg, keeping at least one foot grounded; finish with a soft receiving knee and pelvis facing the original line. No turn or kick; distance at most 1 m.
e.job: Supply forward propulsion before the support leg redirects it into rotation, separating the incoming push from the kick mechanics.
e.gate: Use a shorter step instead if the athlete unintentionally bounds; log any actual flight rather than treating it as grounded.
e.novelty: Rear-leg propulsion into a forward receiving plant, without the jump or hip turn used in other entries.

e.name: Low roundhouse with forward step-down finish
e.execution: From a stationary rear-leg stance, execute a low controlled roundhouse and fold the knee, then place that foot into a short forward split stance instead of returning it to the original rear position. Arrest the pelvis with both feet aligned; no spinning through or second kick.
e.job: Control residual forward/rotational momentum when the kicking leg becomes the next lead foot.
e.gate: Use less kick arc and a shorter step-down instead if the athlete over-rotates or lands across the support foot.
e.novelty: Forward stance-changing recovery rather than the previous return-to-original-base or suspended-chamber finish.

p_jobs: Main strength investment is the forward receiving leg and its drive into the turn.
Control the support hip as forward momentum is arrested.
Preserve lateral/adductor strength to keep the plant from spilling sideways during rotation.
Maintain direct hip torque after a controlled sagittal arrival.
Supply active chamber lift once the forward support leg has accepted weight.
Maintain the bent-knee ankle contribution to the forward plant and heel release.
s_jobs: The supported airplane reinforces pelvic control over the receiving hip; short-foot work supports the forward plant without more impact.
readiness: Forward entry stays short and planned. The athlete must show a soft receiving knee and enough room to stop; no ability is inferred from the preceding linked-contact prescription. Use shorter paths rather than faster approaches.
strength_reason: Retain Class 7 [2,1,1,1,1,1], 88 working reps, with current qualified loads. Same main split-squat investment supports a different force-entry condition; no extra strength volume or predetermined load increase.
exposure_note: Eight landings: four bilateral approach-turn jumps and four opposite-leg forward bounds. Twenty grounded efforts include twelve kicks. E1 has eight approach steps total before its four flights; other entry/recovery contacts are recorded from actual execution rather than inferred as jumps.
space: Limit each complete approach/entry plus action to 2 m, with a separate 2 m recovery area inside one 10 m lane. Forward bounds stay within 1.5 m; the power step stays within 1 m. No joined runway or additional run-off is assumed.
progression: Class 7 offered conditional reactive coupling. This class instead uses short preplanned forward arrivals and fewer landings, without requiring a prior reactive pass. Its forward step-down is a different recovery condition, not evidence of better kick power.
audit: Long accelerations and rotating single-leg landings were rejected. The forward bound stays unturned, while the two-foot approach jump handles rotation. The chamber-only entry limits additional kick extension, and the terminal step-down has a separate momentum-control job.
authoring_handoff: Review Class 8 and real plant/recoil observations, then finalize Class 9 around changing direction and recovering a useful rotational stance; save/audit before continuing.
current_handoff: Record actual delivery/response and review the next saved class against readiness.
